baseRules: Use the uploaded product/image/reference whenever present. Preserve the exact product shape, packaging, label, logo, cap, colors, proportions and brand identity. Make the result feel like a real global advertising campaign, not a generic AI template. Do not default to a bottle standing on a glossy table with a headline on the left, a blurred lifestyle person in the background, random fruit props, pastel gradient panels, mirror/glass walls, symmetrical pedestal compositions, or a soft wellness/spa set. Each new creative must visibly change at least six major design decisions: composition, camera angle, scale, environment, lighting, material language, depth, typography treatment, prop logic, and visual storytelling. No unnecessary headline or body copy unless the user supplied copy or explicitly asked for text. Default output is one standalone 4:5 Instagram creative file per creative. MULTI-PRODUCT RULE: unless the user specifies another quantity, create exactly 2 distinct standalone creative concepts for EACH product. If 6 different products are uploaded, that means 12 separate creatives: Product 1 Creative A and B, Product 2 Creative A and B, and so on. Never combine products or creatives into a collage, grid, contact sheet, split-screen, multi-panel board, or one image containing several requested creatives. Generate/deliver each creative individually as its own image. If multiple uploaded reference images are different angles, close-ups, front/back views, or packaging references of the SAME product, treat them together as references for that one product; do not count each reference image as a separate product. Only place multiple products together in one creative when the user explicitly asks for a bundle, group shot, comparison, range shot, or multi-product composition. When producing 2 creatives for the same product, Creative A and Creative B must use genuinely different concepts/compositions, not just a color or prop change.
families: architecture-scale CGI with monumental spatial forms, dramatic scale and unusual perspective
ingredient world built from the product flavour or ingredient itself, immersive and concept-led
macro surrealism with extreme close-up material detail and unexpected scale relationships
kinetic diagonal composition with directional motion, asymmetry and layered depth
top-down designed scene with precise object choreography and strong negative space
editorial fashion-set art direction with sculptural styling and confident cropping
tactile material concept using one dominant material such as paper, fabric, foam, clay, glass, metal or ice
cinematic narrative frame that feels like a scene from a premium commercial rather than a static poster
product-as-landscape concept where product details, label graphics or flavour become the visual environment
abstract geometry with custom forms, depth and shadows forming a distinct brand world
scientific visualisation with elegant technical or microscopic visual language
real-world action moment with believable motion, hands, environment or consequence instead of passive display
low-angle iconic hero with strong foreshortening, environmental depth and unusual scale
monochrome shadow sculpture using controlled single-colour art direction and sculptural light
fake OOH / impossible scale with an oversized product integrated convincingly into a real location
graphic editorial system driven by cropping, shape, texture and image hierarchy rather than headline-first layout
floating spatial choreography with deliberate depth planes and realistic physics
nature transformed using one specific phenomenon such as mist, mineral, water, stone, sunlight or frost
